destination.question: Which string spectra, interactions, large-central-charge constructions and classical long-string dynamics can support candidate descriptions or completions of AdS3 gravity?
destination.summary: Representation theory, thermal partition functions, winding-sensitive correlators, permutation orbifolds and heavy-string collapse address distinct construction and consistency targets.

systems: Strings on AdS3
Candidate pure AdS3 gravity with boundary gravitons and long strings
Permutation-orbifold CFT constructions

Worldsheet observables, singularities and amplitude factorization
Allowed winding or spectral-flow violation
String-like perturbative degrees of freedom

regimes: Worldsheet and one-loop calculations as specified by each source
Finite large-central-charge spectra in the orbifold question
Probe, light-string and heavy-string regimes kept distinct
Classical heavy strings with gravitational back-reaction
assumptions: The long-string completion assumes the proposed continuous pure-gravity spectrum obeying the Seiberg bound.
Restrictions on permutation orbifolds are necessary-condition questions, not a classification of all holographic CFTs.
The maximally winding-violating correlator question fixes |Δω|=n−2.
conventions: Worldsheet winding and spectral-flow questions retain their source-specific formulations.
Classical collapse is distinguished from quantum nucleation.
String-like perturbative behavior is not automatically an identification with a particular fundamental-string construction.
includes: Comparison of proposed spectra with explicit thermal calculations
excludes: Treating an apparent unflowed-representation mass bound as an established physical constraint
A universal pure-gravity interpretation of light strings
An unconditional existence proof for pure AdS3 quantum gravity

sources.title: Violating the string winding number maximally in Anti-de Sitter space

evidence.text: The original calculation uses Dotsenko-type conjugate vertex representations in H₃⁺/U(1)×R: a Wakimoto β–γ system and background-charged boson, supplemented by spacelike X and timelike T bosons.

sources.title: Long string dynamics in pure gravity on AdS$_{3}$

evidence.text: For heavy strings, applies Israel junction conditions to the discontinuity of shell extrinsic curvature. A large-radius expansion determines a critical-tension condition and mass bound; mixed junction components test the possibility of a rotating exterior.

sources.title: String Universality for Permutation Orbifolds

evidence.text: Group averaging projects the tensor-product Hilbert space onto invariants. Pólya enumeration expresses the untwisted partition function through the cycle index, substituting Z(iτ) for the variable associated with cycles of length i.

sources.title: Strings in AdS(3) and SL(2,R) WZW model 1.: The Spectrum

evidence.text: Bosonize J³ and use parafermions to construct flowed vertex operators and a reflection amplitude. Separately sum spectral-flowed affine characters and analytically continue a Lorentzian partition function to compare with the Euclidean H₃ model.

sources.title: Strings in AdS(3) and the SL(2,R) WZW model. Part 2. Euclidean black hole

evidence.text: Implement thermal winding through twisted boundary conditions labelled by two integers. Integrate the quadratic transverse fields, express the determinant through fermion determinants, and use a chiral gauge transformation and anomaly to obtain the effective shift k → k−2.

sources.title: Strings in AdS(3) and the SL(2,R) WZW model. Part 3. Correlation functions

evidence.text: Expand KZ conformal blocks using hypergeometric functions, combine branches to obtain monodromy invariance, and integrate over the worldsheet cross ratio. Regulate the small-u region before exchanging the modulus and intermediate-spin integrals.

destination.title: AdS3 black-hole spectra and statistical descriptions
destination.question: How can microscopic spectra, refined partition functions and CFT ensembles describe AdS3 black holes and pure gravity, including anomaly-sensitive fermionic spectral statistics?
destination.summary: Entropy calculations, ensemble proposals, number-theoretic probes and fermionic gravity provide different routes to spectral information. Their evidential status and observables remain separate.

systems: AdS3 gravity and two-dimensional CFTs
Fermionic pure gravity defined with spin structures
Ensembles of consistent CFTs, including specified Narain constructions
targets: Black-hole entropy and refined partition functions
Microscopic high-energy spectra
Typicality of gravity-like spectra under a proposed CFT average
Fermionic black-hole states and late-time spectral statistics
Dependence on discrete anomalies
regimes: Higher-derivative and nonperturbative corrections where specified
Leading one- and two-torus-boundary gravitational contributions
assumptions: A normalizable maximum-ignorance measure is a target of the averaging proposal, not an established universal measure.
Fermionic holographic interpretations are proposed; anomaly matching does not exhibit a solvable interacting dual.
Symmetry and anomaly choices determine the relevant fermionic statistical comparisons.
conventions: Microscopic spectra, entropy, spectral correlations and ensemble typicality are different observables.
Free fermions are used to infer anomaly data, not to demonstrate chaotic statistics.
Direct averaging over consistent CFTs is distinct from selecting standard or generalized Narain ensembles.
includes: Number-theoretic methods as a proposed microscopic probe
BTZ counting and mass-gap comparisons from neighboring questions
excludes: An established resolution of all black-hole microstates by L-functions
A claim that free CFTs exhibit the gravitational chaotic statistics
Equating a proposed ensemble description with a proven unique dual CFT

destination.question: When do light-state towers, higher-spin restoration or bounds on higher-spin gaps arise in continuous theory-space limits or specified discrete CFT families, and what controls their rates and bulk interpretation?
destination.summary: A light-spin-two conjecture, information-distance tests, local conformal-manifold arguments and discrete-family gap proposals have different premises. They support a shared direction without defining one distance or one universal tower theorem.

Specified large-central-charge CFT families
targets: Additional light states associated with a light massive spin-two field

assumptions: The spin-two tower proposal is conditional and its admissible AdS tests remain part of the question.
The local conformal-manifold argument uses exactly marginal deformations; its explicit spin-four treatment invokes higher-spin algebra for the broader conclusion.
The supplied exponential-decay condition requires a nonzero controlling descendant three-point-function combination at the higher-spin point.
Discrete-family bounds retain provenance, ordering and averaging assumptions; they are not statements about arbitrary enumerated theories.
conventions: Information distance and Zamolodchikov distance are not identified.
A discrete central-charge increment is not a conformal-manifold distance.
Stepwise gap observations and weighted family bounds are distinct.
Flavor enhancement may occur at finite or infinite distance.

excludes: An unconditional exponential law for every enhancement

A completed definition of all physical CFT families
A proved family gap bound for all unitary CFT sequences

evidence.text: Computes one-loop beta functions and uses Hubbard–Stratonovich large-N saddle points, gap equations, free-energy Hessians and trajectory pullbacks. Distances integrate √Gvv along each selected RG trajectory and sum the steps.

evidence.text: Current-conservation constraints become differential operators on conformal tensor structures. Integrated Ward identities, charge-conservation identities involving the stress tensor, and weakly broken Ward identities combine with Anselmi’s trick to constrain leading behavior near the HS point.

evidence.text: Rewrite the free thermal partition function as a unitary-matrix integral, then integrate Fourier modes of continuous eigenvalue densities at large N. Locate the Hagedorn singularity through loss of positive definiteness of the Gaussian Hessian.

evidence.text: Large-M Schwinger-boson equations are GB(iωn)=[-iωn+λ-ΣB(iωn)]^(-1) and ΣB(τ)=J²GB(τ)²GB(-τ). A complementary fermionic representation changes the self-energy to ΣF(τ)=-J²nb GF(τ)²GF(-τ). Low-frequency power counting and spectral analyticity constrain their solutions.

sources.title: Gapless spin fluid ground state in a random, quantum Heisenberg magnet

evidence.text: Coherent-state path integral, replica disorder averaging, and the N→∞ saddle reduce the problem to self-consistent quantum mechanics of replicated single spins, including the single-spin Berry phase.
